findings.passage: “Today’s decision shows the continued necessity of the Voting Rights Act,” said Rev. Terry Alexander, pastor of Wayside Chapel Baptist Church in Florence and member of the South Carolina House of Representatives. “Because of the VRA’s preclearance provisions, South Carolina had to reinterpret a law that would otherwise have disenfranchised many African Americans. We now urge the state of South Carolina to enforce this law in a way that lives up to its promises in court, ensuring that every South Carolinian, with or without photo ID, can cast a vote that counts. If even one person is disenfranchised because of this law, that will be one person too many.”
findings.note: Quoted in a People For the American Way press release the day after a federal court upheld the state photo ID law but delayed it past the 2012 election. He says the law as first written would have disenfranchised many African Americans, and asks the state to enforce it so voters with or without photo ID can cast a counted vote.

findings.passage: Every legally eligible citizen should be able to vote, stress free and without worry that more stringent voter ID laws are put into place.
findings.note: From the 'Protecting the right to vote' section of his campaign site: says eligible citizens should vote without worry that stricter voter ID laws will be put into place. Page undated.
